resources.string: Observes structural accessibility events only from TikTok, Instagram and YouTube to detect short-video transitions. Scroll Receipt does not read or store video text, captions, comments, messages, images, audio or screenshots.
Counting is automatic. You can close Scroll Receipt; the Android accessibility service keeps listening for supported short-video activity.
Scroll Receipt is not enabled in Accessibility settings. Enable it once before testing.
Accessibility permission is still enabled, but Android stopped the service. Open Accessibility settings and switch Scroll Receipt off, then on again.
Scroll Receipt accessibility service is not active. Open Accessibility settings and restart it before calibration.
Waiting for TikTok, Reels or Shorts

There is no Start button for normal use. Once Accessibility is enabled, Scroll Receipt receives supported Android UI events in the background and counts only when a short-video mode is recognized. Screen off, another app, comments/profile overlays and non-short modes are excluded by the detector.

Normal counting is already running. This section is only for calibration: start one platform, watch a small known number of short videos, enter the real number below, then export the report. The report stores structural Android event metadata only, never video content.
Enter the total number of short videos you actually viewed during this run, including the first visible video.
Target app is not installed or cannot be launched. No calibration was started.
This removes today’s counters and diagnostic logs. It does not disable Accessibility.
Enter a positive manual count before finishing the calibration.
No network permission. No screenshots. No video content, captions, comments, messages, images or audio are stored. Gate 0A keeps only structural event metadata needed to validate the detector.
